boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct, documented Temple University study environments, including quiet, group, technology-focused, and health-sciences options.

cards.title: Charles Library 24/7 Study Area
cards.subtitle: Charles Library, near Liacouras and Polett Walks
cards.notes: Bring a current Temple ID for entry after the library closes; use the printer, laptop kiosk, battery kiosk, or late-return book drop.
cards.short_summary: Round-the-clock Charles Library workspace with practical late-study support.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple Libraries says this Charles Library space is accessible to Temple affiliates 24 hours a day, 365 days a year and includes laptop and battery kiosks plus a printer.
cards.access_notes: Accessible 24 hours a day, 365 days a year to Temple affiliates; after public library closing, swipe a current Temple ID at the Liacouras and Polett Walks entrance.

cards.title: Read Among Current Periodicals
cards.subtitle: Charles Library, third floor
cards.notes: Set up in the open reading room when browsing current journals, magazines, newspapers, or a short fiction break supports your work.
cards.short_summary: Open third-floor reading room beside current periodicals and group-study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple Libraries describes this as an open reading room bordered by private group study rooms and housing current academic journals, magazines, newspapers, and a Short Édition dispenser.
cards.source_title: 3rd Floor Open Reading Area | Temple University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located in Charles Library; the official page also notes it may be requested for special events.

cards.title: Settle Into the Quiet Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Charles Library, fourth floor south side
cards.notes: Choose the enclosed quiet zone for work needing sustained concentration, then use the Bell Tower view as a quick visual reset.
cards.short_summary: Dedicated enclosed quiet zone with a view toward the Bell Tower.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple Libraries identifies the Fourth Floor Quiet Reading Room as a dedicated enclosed quiet zone for concentrated work and says it overlooks the Bell Tower.
cards.source_title: 4th Floor Quiet Reading Room | Temple University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Quiet study is available in the fourth-floor reading room on Charles Library’s south side.

cards.title: Use the Graduate and Faculty Study Area
cards.subtitle: Charles Library, fourth floor
cards.notes: Graduate students and faculty can use this dedicated fourth-floor study area; ask the library about requesting an available locker.
cards.short_summary: Dedicated Charles Library study area for graduate students and faculty.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple Libraries lists a fourth-floor faculty and graduate study area among Charles Library’s study spaces and notes that lockers are available by request.
cards.source_title: Charles Library: What You Need to Know | Temple University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Intended for faculty and graduate students; locker availability is by request.

cards.entity_name: Charles Library Small Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Reserve a Small Room With a Display
cards.subtitle: Charles Library, third and fourth floors
cards.notes: Reserve up to two one-hour blocks in advance, or check for an unreserved room; technology rooms have wireless display connection.
cards.short_summary: Reservable small rooms with table seating; many include flat-screen displays.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple Libraries says Charles small group rooms are on the third and fourth floors, available to Temple students, faculty, and staff, and technology rooms have a table, chairs, and flat-screen display.
cards.source_title: Small Group Study Rooms | Temple University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Temple students, faculty, and staff may reserve up to two one-hour blocks; one reservation per person per day, up to 72 hours ahead.

cards.entity_name: Charles Library Large Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Plan a Session in a Large Group Room
cards.subtitle: Charles Library, third and fourth floors
cards.notes: Use the reservation system for a group work session; if a room is not reserved, it may be available on a first-come basis.
cards.short_summary: Charles Library’s larger reservable rooms for collaborative study.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple Libraries lists large group study rooms as Charles Library study spaces and states that small and large rooms can be reserved ahead or used first-come when unreserved.
cards.access_notes: Most Charles group rooms are on the third and fourth floors; verify availability or reserve before arriving.

cards.entity_name: Ginsburg Health Sciences Library Study Rooms
cards.title: Book a Health Sciences Study Room
cards.subtitle: Ginsburg Health Sciences Library, Medical Education and Research Building
cards.notes: Reserve a small or large room for health-sciences work; small rooms remain unlocked while staff open large rooms when needed.
cards.short_summary: Small and large health-sciences library rooms with a defined booking process.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple Libraries says Ginsburg Health Sciences Library offers small and large group study rooms; reservations are recommended and the rooms are open to Temple affiliates.
cards.source_title: Health Sciences Libraries Study Rooms | Temple University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Open to Temple affiliates. Reservations are recommended; bookings are limited to one three-hour reservation per patron per day, up to 72 hours ahead.

cards.title: Work Near Digital Scholarship Tools
cards.subtitle: Charles Library, third floor
cards.notes: Use this Charles Library studio when a project benefits from high-end computing, makerspace tools, VR equipment, or a creative workshop.
cards.short_summary: Digital-scholarship studio combining creative technology and collaborative work space.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple Libraries describes the Duckworth Scholars Studio as a Charles Library hub for creativity and collaboration with VR equipment, 3D printers, a makerspace, high-end computing, and workshops.
cards.access_notes: Located on Charles Library’s third floor; check with studio staff for current equipment and workshop availability.

cards.title: Use a Fixed Workstation at TECH Center
cards.subtitle: TECH Center, Main Campus
cards.notes: Use a fixed workstation when you need campus software or printing; the orientation guide also lists loaner laptops and specialty printers.
cards.short_summary: Large Main Campus computer-study environment with fixed workstations and printing resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple’s 2025–26 orientation material identifies the TECH Center’s student computer center as having approximately 500 fixed workstations, loaner laptops, and high-speed duplex and color specialty printers.
cards.source_title: 2025–26 First-Year Orientation and Parent/Family Orientation Slides | Temple University
cards.access_notes: Student-focused TECH Center resource; confirm current workstation and printing availability before a time-sensitive visit.

cards.title: Coordinate in a TECH Center Breakout Room
cards.subtitle: TECH Center, Main Campus
cards.notes: Use a breakout room for group study or shared screen work, and check current room availability with TECH Center staff before meeting.
cards.short_summary: Dedicated TECH Center rooms for collaboration and group study.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple’s 2025–26 orientation material states that the TECH Center has 13 breakout rooms and two MediaScape tables for collaboration and group study.
cards.source_title: 2025–26 First-Year Orientation and Parent/Family Orientation Slides | Temple University
cards.access_notes: Part of the student-facing TECH Center; confirm current room procedures and availability before relying on a specific room.
